root_cause.text: The `t7xx_dpmaif_set_frag_to_skb` function adds page fragments to an skb without validating that the current fragment count (`nr_frags`) has not reached `MAX_SKB_FRAGS`, allowing a buffer overflow in the `skb_shinfo(skb)->frags[]` array when the modem firmware supplies excessive fragments.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check (`if (shinfo->nr_frags >= MAX_SKB_FRAGS) return -EINVAL;`) before the call to `skb_add_rx_frag()`, and the commit description explicitly states the function "adds page fragments to an skb without checking if the number of fragments has exceeded MAX_SKB_FRAGS."

Extracts the data length from a modem-supplied header; a malicious firmware could set this to cause multiple calls that exceed MAX_SKB_FRAGS.
